label: Person
name: Cosmo Innes
summary:
Cosmo Innes (1798–1874) was a Scottish historian, antiquary, and lawyer who made fundamental contributions to Scottish historical scholarship — editing and publishing medieval Scottish records that had never previously been systematically accessible. As Advocate-Depute and Professor of Constitutional Law at Edinburgh University, Innes combined legal practice with his passionate historical research. He edited the 'Registrum de Dunfermlyn,' the 'Acts of the Parliaments of Scotland,' and numerous other medieval Scottish documents — creating the archival foundation for modern Scottish historical scholarship.

His 'Sketches of Early Scotch History' (1861) and 'Scotland in the Middle Ages' (1860) were pioneering works that made Scottish medieval history accessible to general educated readers.

His editorial work remains fundamental to Scottish medieval studies.

'The oldest documents speak clearest.'
